entities.name: Gil de Torres
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gil de Torres, a distinguished Leonese cleric and the cardinal-deacon of Santi Cosma e Damiano from 1216 until his death on November 1, 1254, emerged as a pivotal figure in the 13th-century Roman Curia. His nearly four decades at the heart of papal administration, spanning the pontificates of Honorius III, Gregory IX, Celestine IV, and Innocent IV, positioned him as a key advisor and elector during an era defined by the consolidation of papal power, the development of canon law, and intense conflicts with the Holy Roman Empire. Hailing from the Kingdom of León, Gil de Torres' career trajectory underscores the increasing internationalization of the College of Cardinals and the profound influence of legal scholars within the Church’s central governance, shaping its structure and doctrine.

Throughout his cardinalate, Gil de Torres played an instrumental role in several papal elections, most notably the tumultuous Papal Election of 1241, which occurred under severe duress from Emperor Frederick II, and the election of Innocent IV in 1243. He was a close confidant and legal expert to Pope Gregory IX, assisting in the codification of canon law that culminated in the *Decretales Gregorii IX* (Liber Extra), a foundational text for medieval ecclesiastical jurisprudence. His administrative acumen and legal expertise were crucial in navigating the complex diplomatic and theological challenges faced by the Papacy, including the ongoing struggle against the Hohenstaufen emperors for political and spiritual supremacy in Europe.
